To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a salt-tolerate alfalfa cultivar and found that the salt tolerance mechanism of this alfalfa is different with the sensitive alfalfa.
the alfalfa cultivar Zhongmu- 1 is salt-tolerant, and that it maintains a specific physiological status and gene expression profile that confers exceptional salt tolerance.

the alfalfa cultivar Zhongmu- 1 (ZM), which has a higher level of salt tolerance than the cultivar Xingjiang Dayu (XJ), maintains relatively more stable transcript levels of genes related with abiotic and biotical stress response, photosynthesis and growth hormone, which is likely the reason for its superior salt tolerance.

the identification of salt tolerance-related genes and the development of a transcriptome resource that will be useful for alfalfa breeding programs.
the identification and characterization of genes involved in the regulation of alfalfa salt tolerance.
the genetic and transcriptomic mechanisms that underlie salt tolerance in alfalfa and will facilitate the development of alfalfa cultivars with increased salt tolerance.

alfalfa cultivar Zhongmu- 1 is salt-tolerant due to the maintenance of high transcript levels of genes associated with abiotic and biotice stress tolerance and inhibition of plant growth by plant hormones.

the salt-tolerant genotype ZM maintains a relatively stable expression of genes related to stress resistance and growth inhibition, and the salt-sensitive genotype XJ shows more dramatic changes in expression levels of genes involved in stress resistance and growth.

the transcriptome analysis of alfalfa under salt stress revealed the salt tolerance mechanisms of different genotypes.
the alfalfa cultivar Zhongmu- 1 (ZM), which is relatively salt-tolerance, maintains relatively more stable expression of salt resistance-related genes and exhibits stronger tolerance to salt.

alfalfa cultivars with superior salt tolerance can be bred by selecting for specific gene expression patterns.
